title: Cristaux et cohomologie de De Rham : généralités, correspondances Deligne et Berthelot (1965-1969) : notes manuscrites (s.d.), lettre (1965).

deep.reconstruction:
This is a single typewritten page numbered '39 bis', with the archive folio '35' handwritten at the bottom. It is the end of an elementary lemma about almost-additive integer sequences.

Setting (reconstructed from context). φ is a real sequence indexed by positive integers m. It satisfies relation (14), which is off-page but presumably reads |φ(m+n) − φ(m) − φ(n)| ≤ d for all m, n. Put ψ(m) = φ(m)/m.

Claim. The limit a = lim ψ(m) exists, and |φ(m) − a·m| ≤ d for all m.

Step 1, convergence. The preceding page (not shown) presumably bounds |ψ(m) − ψ(m')| by ε for m, m' large, with ε and m₀ fixed. The page opens by concluding that ψ is Cauchy, hence convergent, with limit a.

Step 2, normalisation. Replace φ(m) by φ(m) − a·m. This sequence satisfies (14) with the same constant d, and its ψ tends to 0. So it suffices to show: if a = 0 then |φ(m)| ≤ d for all m.

Step 3, doubling. Relation (14) with n = m gives |φ(2m) − 2φ(m)| ≤ d. Induction on h then gives |φ(2^h m) − 2^h φ(m)| ≤ (2^h − 1)d.

Step 4, contradiction. Suppose φ(m₁) = d₁ > d. Then φ(2^h m₁) ≥ 2^h d₁ − (2^h − 1)d > (2^h − 1)(d₁ − d). Hence ψ(2^h m₁) stays above roughly (d₁ − d)/m₁ > 0 and does not tend to 0, contradicting a = 0.

In modern terms, this is homogenization of a quasimorphism on ℕ (or ℤ). The homogenized limit a·m is the unique additive function at bounded distance from φ, and the distance is at most the defect d. This is Hyers–Ulam stability for the additive Cauchy equation, or equivalently the Pólya–Szegő/Fekete-type subadditivity argument.

Context. The page has nothing to do with crystals or de Rham cohomology. The previous page is handwritten notes on divided-power relations Γ^n(λ). The next page is handwritten notes on the Poincaré lemma for singular k-algebras, with a journal note 'Ann. Éc. N. Sc. [65 ou 66] ou J. de Liouville'. This is plausibly a stray page of a typed manuscript. It could be by Grothendieck or by someone else; it might come from a paper on growth or heights, where bounded-defect additive functions occur, as with Néron–Tate heights. Nothing on the page itself decides this.
errors: Gap: the page only treats the case φ(m₁) = d₁ > d. The symmetric case φ(m₁) < −d is needed for the stated bound |φ(m)| ≤ d. It follows by the same argument applied to −φ, but this is not said.
The bound (2^h − 1)(d₁ − d) is weaker than what the induction actually gives (2^h d₁ − (2^h − 1)d). It is still sufficient: ψ(2^h m₁) ≥ (1 − 2^{-h})(d₁ − d)/m₁ does not tend to 0.
The statement of relation (14) and the Cauchy estimate lie on the preceding typed page, which is not available. The convergence step cannot be checked here.

ideas.what: For a sequence with bounded additivity defect d, φ(m)/m converges to some a, and |φ(m) − a·m| ≤ d (proof by doubling and contradiction).
ideas.modern_name: Hyers–Ulam stability of the Cauchy equation / homogenization of quasimorphisms
ideas.usually_credited_to: Pólya–Szegő (problem book, 1925); D. H. Hyers (1941); folklore
ideas.where_published: Standard in analysis texts and in quasimorphism / bounded cohomology literature; also used for Néron–Tate canonical heights (Tate's limit argument)

ideas.what: Reduction to the case a = 0 by subtracting the linear part a·m.
ideas.modern_name: normalization of a quasimorphism to its homogenization

deep.surprise_reason: This is a routine, classical elementary lemma (Hyers–Ulam / quasimorphism homogenization), typed as part of some manuscript and apparently misfiled among crystalline-cohomology notes. It contains nothing new. The only curiosity is archival: its presence in this folder and its unknown source manuscript.
transcription_corrections: The page carries the archive folio '35' handwritten at the bottom left; the transcription's '35' is that number and is not part of the text.
'Ceci' was typed as 'Cæci'/'Ceci' with a correction over-strike. The typed word is 'contredirait' (sic, for 'contredirait'/'contredirait l'hypothèse'); it is correctly transcribed.
In 'ψ(2^h m₁) = φ(2^h m₁)/2^h m₁' the denominator is 2^h m₁ (product), as transcribed.
